# Bot builder instructions

<!-- Generated by build.sh from skills/*/SKILL.md - edit those, then run ./build.sh -->

Follow both parts below in every task on this project.


# Working with this builder

They build Telegram sales bots (VPN shops on Marzban/Rebecca-type panels, with wallets,
gateways, renewals, referrals) and the web panels and installers around them, and they reuse the
same habits on every new bot. They are not a programmer by trade: they judge the result by
using the bot. So results must work when tapped, and explanations must make sense to someone
who sees menus, not code.

## Talking to them

- Reply in **Persian**, fluent and friendly, plain words. Code, file names and commands stay as
  they are.
- Before long work, one line on what you are about to do; while working, a short line now and
  then on what you are doing. No long recaps.
- When something is done: what changed (in their words: which menu, which button), how it was
  tested, what was *not* tested and why, and what they need to do (if anything). Be honest; if
  a voice was synthetic, a payment was only tested against a mock, or a bug might remain, say it.
- Give paths the way they navigate: `🏬 تنظیمات فروشگاه ← 🛒 وضعیت قابلیت‌های فروشگاه ← ⚙️ …`.
- They care about token cost: do not spawn helper agents or re-read huge files without need;
  prefer targeted searches.
- If they answer "اره ولش کن" (forget it), drop that thread completely.
- A decision that is theirs (a repository name, public or private, turning something on by
  default, deleting data) is asked, briefly, with a recommendation. Everything else: decide and do.

## Product taste

- **Everything customizable, per language.** Every customer-facing text and button can be edited
  from the bot's 🎨 menu and from the web panel, separately per language, with premium emoji,
  stickers and button colours. Use the `telegram-bot-customization` skill for how.
- **New features are off by default**, each with its own switch (per language), and with
  sub-switches for the risky parts (for example "keep the gateway's min/max" or "gift on
  direct payment" - both off until the admin turns them on).
- **Three places for every feature:** the bot's admin menu, the web panel, and 🎨. A feature only
  in one of them is not finished.
- **Admin texts are Persian only.** Customer texts exist in every supported language (Persian
  and English); no English inside Persian screens and no Persian left in English ones.
- **Friendly colloquial Persian** in bot texts ("کدوم بخش رو می‌خوای تنظیم کنی؟"), emoji at the
  start of buttons and headings, `<blockquote>` for explanations, `<b>` for amounts and names,
  `<code>` for anything to copy.
- **Telegram behaviour they expect:** move through a flow by editing the same message; the back
  button sits below and returns exactly one step; a toggle flips at once with no confirmation and
  shows its state (✅ green / ❌ red); stale messages are removed; old buttons answer with a clear
  alert; no message silently vanishes; no duplicate messages.
- **Web panel:** dark glass look, Vazirmatn font, right to left, SVG line icons for the panel's
  own chrome, saves without reloading, lists refresh by themselves, date-range filters on every
  list, every ID clickable to the profile, works on a phone, gentle motion (reduced-motion
  respected).
- **Money must be exact:** a purchase, a renewal or a top-up is settled (invoice active, wallet
  changed, payment marked) the moment the external service confirms; a second tap, a second
  approval or a webhook retry never charges, credits or builds twice; failures refund to the
  wallet and say so; min/max limits and gifts follow the admin's settings; every money event is
  reported to the admin group in its topic.
- **Beginner admins:** after every change set, a "what's new" entry the admin sees in the bot:
  what it is, a concrete example, on/off by default, and the step-by-step path (1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣),
  plus the web panel path.

## Engineering habits

- Read the code that is there before adding to it; extend the existing mechanism instead of
  creating a second one. Keep compatibility with the original upstream bot and its database
  (an old backup must restore and upgrade itself).
- Database changes are idempotent ("add column if missing") and also applied lazily at first use.
- Test on a local rig before pushing: the real code with a fake Telegram API that logs every
  call, fake panel and gateway APIs, a real database; drive it with scripted taps; crawl the
  menus and read the PHP error log; load every web panel page in a headless browser. Report the
  results, including what failed.
- Debugging means finding the real cause and showing it (the line, the order of operations),
  not adding retries around it. Fix what you can prove; list what you suspect.
- Git: commit with a message that explains why; push to the branches the project uses (often
  the main branch and a working branch together); never force-push; no pull request unless asked;
  do not bump the version number unless asked; never rewrite tags or releases.
- Never weaken security to make something work (no disabled TLS checks, no secrets in code or
  in chat); passwords shown in screenshots or videos are masked.

## Tutorials and media

When they ask for a tutorial video: Persian narration in a natural, warm tone with burned-in
subtitles, section by section with a chapter list, real screens of the bot recorded from the
rig, sensitive values masked. Say plainly if the voice is synthetic and that you could not
listen to it yourself.

# Telegram bot customization (🎨)

The idea in one sentence: **nothing a customer sees is hard-wired.** Every message and every
button has a stable key, a default text per language, and an optional per-language override that
the admin edits from a 🎨 menu inside the bot (and the same data from a web panel). A new feature
is not finished until its texts and buttons are in that system.

This came out of building a large Telegram shop bot (Ciro) where the owner kept asking for "this
should be editable too" one screen at a time. Building it in from the start is far cheaper than
retrofitting 160 messages later, so treat it as part of every feature, not as an extra.

## When you start on a bot

1. Find (or create) the text layer: one file per language with nested keys
   (`users.Balance.shortLine`, `users.sell.service_sell`). No customer text inline in code.
2. Find (or create) the override store and the resolver (see `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/data-model.md`).
3. Find (or create) the registry: the single list that says which keys and button groups appear
   in 🎨, under which group and section, with which admin label.
4. Read `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/checklist.md` before calling any feature done.

If the bot already has some of this under other names, use what exists and extend it. Do not
build a second parallel system.

## The five things that must be editable

| What | Per language | Stored as | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Message text | yes | override text, or none = default | keep placeholders like `{price}` working; HTML or entities |
| Message extras | yes | sticker file_id, reaction emoji, media | sticker is sent before the message and removed when that screen is replaced |
| Buttons of a message | yes | per (message key, button index): name, emoji, premium emoji id, emoji side, plain mode, colour, hidden | back / close buttons can be restyled but never hidden |
| Layout | yes | order of buttons and how many per row | the "📐 چیدمان" editor |
| Feature switches | yes, unless truly global | `feature[lang][key]` | new features default to **off** |

Admin-only texts (the admin menus themselves) do not need per-language overrides; they live in
the admin's language only. Customer texts always exist in every supported language.

## Resolution rules (get these right first)

- `text(key, lang)` = override for (lang, key) if non-empty, else the default text of that
  language, else the default of the primary language. Never return an empty string: Telegram
  refuses empty messages, and a blank bubble looks broken.
- Everything is resolved in the **receiver's** language. A message to a referrer, an approval
  result sent to a customer by an admin, a cron notice: use the recipient's language and their
  overrides, not the language of whoever triggered the request.
- A change on one language tab never changes another language. If something must be shared
  (one payment-processor account for all languages), mark it visibly (🌐) on every tab.
- Buttons are built through one function (`render(def, override, callback)`), so colour, emoji,
  premium emoji and hiding work the same on every screen. Do not hand-build buttons for customer
  screens.
- Overrides are data, never code. Validate on save: placeholders that the default has must still
  be there (warn, do not silently break), HTML must be balanced, length within Telegram limits.

## The 🎨 menu the admin sees

Main screen: language tabs on top (`✅🇮🇷 فارسی | 🇬🇧 English`), then groups. White header buttons
are section titles (tapping one only shows a short alert explaining that section). A green
button means "this item is customized"; a legend explains the markers:
`✏️ text changed  ❤️ has reaction  🖼 has sticker  🔘 buttons changed`. At the bottom:
`🔁 reset all to default` (with confirmation) and `❌ close`.

Item screen (one message):

```
📝 <b>👋 متن خوش‌آمدید</b>
➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖
✏️ متن: پیش‌فرض
🖼 استیکر: ندارد ❌
❤️ ری‌اکشن: ندارد ❌
➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖
👁 <b>متن فعلی:</b>
<blockquote>سلام خوش آمدید</blockquote>
👇 بخشی که می‌خوای تنظیم کنی رو انتخاب کن:
[📋 کپشن پیش‌فرض] [✏️ ویرایش کپشن]
[🖼 استیکر] [❤️ ری‌اکشن]
[🔘 دکمه‌های این پیام]
[🔁 ریست همه‌ی تنظیمات این پیام]
[🔙 بازگشت به منوی قبل] [🔙 برگشت به لیست]
[❌ بستن]
```

Editing a text: the admin sends the new text; premium emoji and formatting are kept (store the
entities or convert them to `<tg-emoji emoji-id="…">` HTML). Show the placeholders this text
supports right in the prompt. After saving, redraw the item screen in place (edit the same
message).

Button screen: list the message's buttons; for each: rename, emoji (normal or premium), emoji
side (start/end), plain (no emoji), colour (`success` green / `danger` red / `primary` blue /
default), hide/show (not for back/close), reset. Show state, not action: a hidden button shows
"🙈 پنهان", not "show".

Layout screen (📐): the buttons in their current rows; tap one to select, then move it
up/down/left/right or change how many sit in a row. Items added later (a new feature button)
must appear in the layout automatically, at a sensible default position, and must be movable.

More detail, including every screen and callback naming, in `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/admin-screens.md`.

## Feature switches

- A features screen per scope: "global" (whole bot) and "per language" (this tab only). Each row
  is `[✅ روشن | name]` or `[❌ خاموش | name]`, green/red, and one tap flips it and redraws the
  same message. No confirmation step for a plain on/off.
- Every new feature ships **off**. Turning it on must never change what existing customers see
  until the admin decides.
- A feature with its own settings gets a `⚙️ تنظیمات …` button next to its switch, and its hub
  repeats the language tabs.

## Web panel parity

Whatever the bot's 🎨 can edit, the web panel can edit too, from the same registry and the same
store, so the two never disagree. Pages: texts (group tabs, search, "only customized" filter,
sticker id field), buttons, looks/layout (drag to reorder, live preview), features (cards with
switches). Save without reloading the page (fetch + toast), show the new state immediately. See
`skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/web-panel.md`.

## Telegram UI conventions that go with it

- Edit the current message in place when moving between screens of one flow; send a new message
  only when the old one cannot become the new one (media type change, a sticker in between).
- Remove stale screens (an invoice that was paid, a menu that was replaced) so nothing old can be
  tapped. If an old button is tapped anyway, answer with an alert and a way forward, not a crash
  or a silent no-op.
- Navigation buttons at the bottom: `🔙 back` (red or default), `❌ close`. Confirm buttons green.
- `<blockquote>` for notes and explanations, `<b>` for the values that matter, `<code>` for
  anything the user may copy (IDs, links, amounts).
- Errors and refusals: `answerCallbackQuery` with `show_alert` for short ones; a short message
  with the fix for longer ones. Never "unknown error".
- Every list that can grow: paging, and search when long.

## Before you say it is done

Run through `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/checklist.md`. In short: texts in every language, registry entry, 🎨
item opens and edits, buttons through the shared renderer, switch defaults off, web panel shows
it, receiver-language checked, test on a rig with a fake Telegram API, and a "what's new" note
for the admin that says where to find it (menu path, step by step).

## Reference: done checklist


Copy this into your notes and tick it honestly.

- [ ] Every new customer text exists in **every** language file (no English left in Persian
      screens, no Persian in English ones).
- [ ] Admin-only texts are in the admin language file only.
- [ ] Each new text has a registry entry (label, key, group, section) and opens in 🎨 on every
      language tab; edit, sticker, reaction and reset work.
- [ ] New buttons go through the shared renderer and belong to a button group; rename, emoji,
      premium emoji, colour, hide and layout work; back/close cannot be hidden.
- [ ] The new button shows up in 📐 layout and can be moved.
- [ ] Texts and extras are resolved in the receiver's language (crons, admin actions, referrals).
- [ ] A new feature has a switch, per language unless truly global, **off by default**.
- [ ] The web panel can see and change everything the bot can for this feature.
- [ ] Stale buttons from old messages answer with a clear alert, never a PHP/Python error.
- [ ] Money paths are idempotent: a second tap, a second approval or a retried webhook never
      charges, credits or builds twice; state is saved right after the external call succeeds.
- [ ] Tested on a local rig: fake Telegram API that logs calls, fake panel/payment APIs, a real
      database; menus crawled for errors in the log.
- [ ] A what's-new entry for the admin, beginner friendly, with the menu path and the default.
